## 7.1 One main chip: the SoC

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A phone puts its main parts on one chip, the system on a chip (SoC).
- The SoC holds the CPU cores, the GPU, the NPU, the modem and more.
- The CPU and the GPU share the RAM, so a phone has no separate video memory.
- **Do it:** Find the model of your phone in Settings. Which SoC does it have?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/soc-map.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Inside the SoC

a) Which part of the SoC draws every frame of a racing game?
b) Which part sends the score to the online leaderboard over 4G?
c) Where does the GPU of a phone keep its textures?

::: {.answer}
a) the GPU
b) the modem
c) in the RAM that it shares with the CPU
:::

## 7.2 Sensors feel the player

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The accelerometer feels gravity, so it shows how the phone is tilted or shaken.
- The gyroscope shows how fast the phone turns, and it reads 0 when the phone is still.
- The GPS finds the position, and the compass finds north.
- **Do it:** Open Tilt Lab on your phone and lay the phone flat. What does the accelerometer show on z?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/sensors.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 2 · Which sensor?

a) Which sensor does a racing game use when the player steers by tilting the phone?
b) Which sensor does a shooter use when the player aims by turning the phone?
c) A tilted phone lies still on a book. Which sensor reads 0?

::: {.answer}
a) the accelerometer
b) the gyroscope
c) the gyroscope
:::

## 7.3 How the screen feels a finger

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A capacitive touch screen has a grid of thin wires under the glass.
- The finger changes the charge where it touches, so cloth gloves do not work.
- The touch sampling rate says how often the screen checks for touches, for example 240 times per second.
- **Do it:** Draw on your phone with a fingertip, a fingernail and a pencil. Which ones work?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/touch-grid.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3 · The touch screen

a) Why does a normal glove not work on a touch screen?
b) At 240 Hz, how often does the screen check for touches?
c) A sheet says "60 Hz" and "touch 120 Hz". What does each number tell?

::: {.answer}
a) Cloth does not carry the charge of the finger.
b) about every 4 ms
c) The picture changes 60 times per second; touches are checked 120 times per second.
:::

## 7.4 Battery and heat

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The battery capacity is in mAh, and a game draws a current in mA.
- The play time is about the capacity divided by the current.
- A hot SoC slows down by itself, and the frame rate drops: thermal throttling.
- **Do it:** Open the battery page in Settings. Which three apps used the most battery today?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/battery.png)
:::
::::

## Example · Play time

The test phone has a 5000 mAh battery.
**How long can the player play at 1000 mA, and at 800 mA?**

::: {.reveal}
1. At 1000 mA the play time is 5000 ÷ 1000 = **5 hours**.
2. At 800 mA, with a darker screen, it is 5000 ÷ 800, about **6 hours**.
3. A battery saver mode at 30 fps also keeps the phone cooler.
:::

## Live demo · Battery Lab

{{< sim file="sims/battery-lab.html" poster="sims/battery-lab.png" title="Battery Lab: play time and heat" task="**Show:** switch from 60 fps to 120 fps and high graphics, then to 30 fps. **Ask:** which setting changes the play time most, and when does the phone get hot?" >}}

## Try it 4 · Battery and heat

a) A phone has 4500 mAh, and a game draws 900 mA. About how long can the player play?
b) The SoC is hot after 20 minutes. What happens to the game?
c) Does a bigger mAh number make a phone faster?

::: {.answer}
a) about 5 hours
b) The SoC slows down, and the frame rate drops (thermal throttling).
c) No: the battery only holds more charge.
:::

## Game challenge · Marble Peak

{{< sim file="sims/marble-peak.html" poster="sims/marble-peak.png" title="Marble Peak: tilt to roll the marble" kind="game" task="**The story:** Byte Bay tests Marble Peak, a tilt game, on its phone T1 with a 5000 mAh battery. **Play:** tilt your phone (or use the pad) to collect the gems and reach the goal." >}}

## Try it 5 · Problems in the test (harder)

The facts: Marble Peak reads the accelerometer. On T1 (5000 mAh) it draws 1000 mA, and it falls to 45 fps after 20 minutes.

a) Why does the game fall to 45 fps after 20 minutes?
b) A tester's phone has no gyroscope. Can the tester play Marble Peak?
c) In battery saver mode the game draws 800 mA. How long does T1 last?

::: {.answer}
a) The hot SoC slows down (thermal throttling).
b) Yes: the game uses the accelerometer.
c) about 6 hours (5000 ÷ 800)
:::

## Summary

- The SoC holds the CPU cores, the GPU, the NPU and the modem, and it shares the RAM.
- The accelerometer shows the tilt, and the gyroscope shows the turning.
- A capacitive touch screen finds the charge of a finger.
- The play time is about the battery capacity divided by the current.
- A hot SoC slows down, so a lower frame rate saves power and heat.
